airport.name: Kinston Regional Jetport At Stallings Field

summary: Kinston Regional Jetport at Stallings Field (ISO/KISO) is a public airport about 3 miles north of downtown Kinston, North Carolina. Originally a World War II Army Air Forces training field, it now supports general aviation, corporate, cargo, and military operations alongside the adjacent North Carolina Global TransPark. Its 11,500-foot runway is among the longest in eastern North Carolina, making it capable of handling large aircraft.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Kinston Regional Jetport?
A: Scheduled commercial airline service is limited or not currently offered; the airport mainly handles general aviation, corporate, cargo, and military flights. Check current status before booking.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Kinston?
A: It is about 3 miles north of downtown Kinston, roughly a 10-minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: What is the main runway at KISO?
A: Runway 5/23 is 11,500 feet long, allowing it to accommodate large aircraft and serving as a useful alternate in eastern North Carolina.

Q: Are rental cars or rideshare available at the airport?
A: Rental car and rideshare options can be limited, so arrange transportation in advance or confirm availability with the FBO/terminal before arrival.
transport_tips: The airport is easiest to reach by car, a short drive from downtown Kinston via US 70 and NC 11. Taxi and rideshare availability may be limited, so pre-arrange a pickup or rental car. For more flight options, consider Raleigh-Durham (RDU) or Greenville (PGV), both larger airports within driving distance.
local_tip: Frequent visitors know the terminal is compact and parking is usually easy, but if you're heading to the Global TransPark, confirm the specific building entrance—some TransPark addresses are closer via Airport Road than through downtown Kinston.
